{"predictors": [
{"name": "Capital Expenditure Stability", "construction": "Calculate the standard deviation of capital expenditures (Compustat #30) over the past 5 years, then scale by the average total assets (Compustat #6) over the same period", "rationale": "Firms with stable capital expenditures are better equipped to handle economic downturns, as they have a more predictable cost structure. This stability can lead to more consistent cash flows and higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Accounts Receivable Turnover Acceleration", "construction": "Calculate the year-over-year change in accounts receivable turnover (Compustat #2 / Compustat #12) over the past 3 years", "rationale": "An increase in accounts receivable turnover indicates improving operational efficiency and potentially higher profitability, leading to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Research and Development Intensity Volatility", "construction": "Calculate the standard deviation of research and development expenses (Compustat #46) as a percentage of sales (Compustat #12) over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with volatile R&D intensity may be taking on excessive risk, leading to lower returns, while those with stable R&D intensity can more reliably generate innovation and growth", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Inventory Growth Deceleration", "construction": "Calculate the year-over-year decrease in inventory growth (Compustat #3) over the past 2 years", "rationale": "A deceleration in inventory growth can indicate improving operational efficiency, as firms are better managing their inventory levels and reducing waste", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Trend in Earnings Surprise", "construction": "Calculate the slope of the earnings surprise (actual earnings per share - consensus earnings per share) over the past 4 quarters, using data from IBES", "rationale": "A positive trend in earnings surprise indicates a firm's ability to consistently exceed expectations, leading to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Short Interest Momentum", "construction": "Calculate the year-over-year change in short interest (number of shares short) over the past 2 years, using data from the NYSE", "rationale": "An increase in short interest can indicate growing skepticism about a firm's prospects, leading to lower returns, while a decrease can indicate improving sentiment and higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Dividend Yield Dispersion", "construction": "Calculate the standard deviation of dividend yields (annual dividend per share / stock price) over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with stable dividend yields are more likely to have a stable cash flow stream, leading to higher returns, while those with high dispersion may be experiencing cash flow uncertainty", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Employee Growth Rate", "construction": "Calculate the year-over-year growth rate in the number of employees (Compustat #29) over the past 3 years", "rationale": "Firms with high employee growth rates may be experiencing rapid expansion and improving operational efficiency, leading to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Property, Plant, and Equipment Renewal Rate", "construction": "Calculate the ratio of capital expenditures (Compustat #30) to gross property, plant, and equipment (Compustat #7) over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with high renewal rates are more likely to have modern and efficient production facilities, leading to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Director and Officer Ownership Concentration", "construction": "Calculate the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) of director and officer ownership (number of shares owned by each director and officer) over the past 2 years, using data from Compact Disclosure", "rationale": "Firms with concentrated ownership among directors and officers may have more aligned incentives and better governance, leading to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}
]}
